The Financial Analyst Memo: every financial table and model output behind this memo

Teleperformance: a flat, cash-rich business priced as a shrinking one, with the proof that could re-rate it dated no earlier than late 2027

For Richard. Written 2026-11-13. Share price EUR 71.68 (2026-11-11). Forecasts from the Financial Analyst's model (update 2), unchanged (end notes).

#0Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

The case in one paragraph. Teleperformance, the largest outsourced customer-service operator in the world, trades at about five times earnings, the first percentile of its own ten-year range. A multiple of five times implies that earnings shrink by 7-9% a year for ever (my arithmetic, #11). The forecasts say earnings stay flat, with an 18% free cash flow yield. The gap between those two readings is the investment case. What stands between the gap and the share price is proof, and the proof comes late. Over the next six to nine months, cuts to estimates are more likely than upgrades. The first hard evidence that the business is flat rather than shrinking arrives between late July and early November 2027.

The implication for your decisionThe risk/reward is attractive in size but not yet skewed in timing: the negative news is front-loaded and dated, the positive news is back-loaded and mostly mechanical, and the results of 2027-02-25 are the first day on which the setup can be judged.

The seven things that matter

  1. Teleperformance is not yet an upgrade situation, and I can date when it could become one. Guidance and estimate changes are skewed negative to July 2027 and turn neutral-to-positive after that (#7). The news flow is U-shaped: the negatives come first and are dated; the positives come later and are mostly mechanical.
  2. The operating base is steadier than the narrative suggests. Outside Trust & Safety (T&S, the content-moderation vertical), the group has grown +1.7% to +2.0% in each period of 2026. T&S, the source of the 2026 shock, is now under 4% of revenue. Costs are variable, and no client is more than 6% of revenue (#1, #3).
  3. The operating base does not grow, so all EPS growth comes from below the operating line. Of the EUR 1.94 rise in clean EPS from FY2026 to FY2029, falling restructuring contributes 56%, falling interest 32%, a lower share count 15%, and operations slightly less than nothing (#6).
  4. The board, not the business, sets FY2027 earnings. The board announces the restructuring guide and the capital plan on two occasions: the FY2026 results (2027-02-25) and a strategic update in the first half of 2027 (#2, #4).
  5. Price is the risk, not volume. One point of Core Services price given back and not matched by productivity costs about 8% of EPS; one point of volume costs about 2.5% (#9).
  6. The multiple is nine-tenths of the model's return. At the guideline fair multiple of 18.89 times, the model shows +292.5% to end-2027. Each turn of the multiple is worth EUR 14.4 a share, 20% of today's price. I judge that the evidence supports 5-7 times within 18 months, which gives +17% to +53% if earnings arrive as forecast, against about -17% at a trough multiple of 3.5 times (#11, #12).
  7. Three tests at the FY2026 results on 2027-02-25 decide whether Teleperformance becomes one of your setups (checklist below; #4, #7).

The five judgements that move the value most (arithmetic in #9)

Where I differ from the market

(a)On the shape of the AI damage: I see price creep through annual renewals as the base case, and a cliff as a tail risk.
(b)On timing: the T&S drag on growth does not lapse until the third quarter of 2027, later than the loose "2027" in the market narrative.
(c)On FY2027 EPS: FY2027 EPS growth is a board decision about restructuring, which nobody states.
(d)On disposals: the first transaction worth having is the small one (TLScontact, visa services), not the large one.
(e)On the multiple: the fair multiple is far below the guideline's 18.89 times and modestly above the five times the price implies.

#1The operating environment: a broad headwind on price, and only narrow tailwinds

Conclusion: the environment is a strong, broad headwind on price with only narrow, mechanical tailwinds (the T&S base effect from the second half of 2027, weaker delivery currencies, vendor consolidation), so it caps the case at "flat" and gives no help to upgrades.

Evidence.

  • Price. Clients are repricing the core product, a human agent billed by the hour or by the seat, downwards on every measure in channel checks to November 2026 (the four figures above). Offshoring takes a further 1.5 points a year off revenue, although it helps the margin percentage.
  • Automation of T&S. T&S fell from 8.0% of revenue in FY2025 to 5.5% in the first nine months of 2026, and it caused half of the guidance cut of 2026-11-05.
  • Voice. End-to-end speech models now respond within the 200 milliseconds of human turn-taking (Jefferies, 2026-09-12). BBVA's voice assistant resolved close to 90% of pilot interactions, and Tata Capital cut its servicing cost per call by 75%. Global call-centre employment was falling 4.1% a year by mid-2026 (Morgan Stanley).
  • Wages. Labour costs in the delivery hubs are rising by statute. Metro Manila added PHP 60 a day from September 2026, with a further PHP 25 contested for January 2027. Colombia's minimum wage rose 23% for 2026 against a budget assumption of 7.5%; the 2027 decree is due in late December 2026 (Morgan Stanley assumes 8.3%; the main union asks for far more).
  • The narrow tailwinds. Clients are cutting vendor panels in favour of scaled, well-capitalised providers. The Philippine peso is at a record low (64.20 to the dollar) and the Indian rupee is down 7.5% in twelve months, which lowers the dollar cost of delivery once twelve-month hedges roll off. Private buyers have paid 12.0 times EV/EBITDA for unlisted business-services companies against 9.1 times for listed ones (Morgan Stanley, 2026-05-11), which supports the value of the Specialized Services assets.
  • Markets. The backdrop is unfriendly to a leveraged French equity: the French ten-year yield is above 5%, and its spread to Germany is 174 basis points.

Inference: three things follow from the evidence.

  1. The AI damage arrives as creep, with an occasional step. The creep is about 2-4% of revenue a year through renewals, and it is already in the forecasts (net price of -2 to -2.5 points of Core Services revenue a year, against volume of +2.5 to 3 points). A step loss is not in the forecasts.
  2. The T&S collapse cannot repeat at scale. The T&S work that remains is small, and it is the sensitive work that resists automation (Morgan Stanley).
  3. Currency is the one external force that has moved in Teleperformance's favour since the summer, and the market narrative barely mentions it. On the company's stated sensitivities (a 10% move in the peso is worth 3.6% of EPS, in the rupee 3.0%), the moves since the summer are worth about 3-5% of EPS gross, or 0.3-0.5 point of margin (my arithmetic), before clients and wage boards take their share. History says clients and wage boards take much of it: the same currencies added 40 basis points to the margin in FY2022, while Indian IT-services companies saw a similar gain competed away in 2012. The model banks only 10-20 basis points.
So what. The environment offers no tailwind to revenue. It caps like-for-like growth near +1% and turns the margin into a contest between price concessions and savings. The forecast needs the environment outside T&S to be no worse than in 2026. It does not need the environment to improve.
Strongest counter-case. Bear: voice goes the way of content moderation, fast, and across several top-ten clients (31% of revenue) at once. Morgan Stanley's bear scenario of revenue falling 5% a year at an 11% margin values the shares at EUR 10.
Bull: consumer AI agents multiply the number of customer contacts, and scaled, compliant operators own the human escalation layer; over 70% of Teleperformance's new deals in 2026 already include an AI solution.

What would change my view. Worse: growth outside T&S at or below zero for two quarters; the loss of a programme from a top-ten client; a double-digit Colombian wage decree; a US tax on offshored services (the HIRE Act proposal, which I judge low-probability). Better: growth outside T&S of +1.5% or more in Q4 2026 and Q1 2027; a slowing of the decline in call-centre headcount; Concentrix guiding to stable margins in mid-January 2027.

Against the market. The market prices a cliff: Morgan Stanley values the group at a 16% discount rate with zero terminal growth. I agree with the market on the direction of the AI damage and disagree on its shape. The evidence shows creep, which an operator with variable costs can absorb; I put the probability of a cliff at 15-25% over 18 months. I also date the T&S base effect more precisely than the market. T&S stepped down again in Q3 2026, so it still takes about 2.8 points off group growth in H1 2027 and nothing in H2 2027. Reported revenue growth therefore stays negative until the Q3 2027 release in early November 2027, and investors expecting relief from the first quarter of 2027 will be disappointed in April and July.

Score: 18, set by the Rater. The core product is being repriced down by a substitute that is still advancing: 2-5% price pressure on renewals and 3-7% on rebids, T&S automated outright (8.0% to under 4% of revenue), voice (64% of interactions) next, statutory wage rises in Manila and Colombia, while the tailwinds (weaker peso and rupee, vendor consolidation) are narrow and largely competed away; consensus sales growth at the 10.7th percentile and EPS growth at the 10.9th tell the truth, and the T&S base effect from H2 2027 is arithmetic, not a force. A structural, still-building headwind that caps the business at flat, coherent with the group's 20, between BP 22 and Imperial Brands 16, above Maersk because the damage arrives as creep a variable-cost operator can absorb rather than a collapse.

#2Internally driven corporate change: a new team that has repaired costs and capital, but not revenue

Conclusion: corporate change is strong in people, cost and capital discipline and absent from the revenue engine, so it supports a held earnings base and an option on capital allocation, not an earnings step-up.

Evidence. The top of the company was replaced in eight months.

  • The founder, Daniel Julien, stepped down on 2026-03-15 after nearly 50 years. Jorge Amar, who spent 14 years at McKinsey and has no profit-and-loss experience in the industry, became chief executive the next day.
  • The chairman, Moulay Hafid Elalamy, is now separate from the chief executive. His Saham Group took economic exposure to about 15% of the company through a swap of up to EUR 355 million.
  • The finance director, the head of Specialized Services and a new Chief AI Officer are all 2026 appointments.

Inference. The corporate change is real and large, and it sits entirely in what management controls: cost, tax, financing and capital. It has not touched what clients pay. The FY2026 guide itself proves the point, in three steps:

Step 1The FY2026 margin target stayed at 14.6% while the savings target rose.
Step 2The implied second-half margin is slightly below last year's, despite EUR 75-85 million of savings landing.
Step 3Underlying erosion is therefore about 1.7 points of revenue a year, and the savings only just cover it.
ImplicationSelf-help is a treadmill: it holds the margin and does not raise it.

The year-on-year help from the savings programme ends after H1 2027, because from then both halves of the comparison carry the full run-rate of savings.

So what. Corporate change gives the case a floor, not a step-up. It explains why recurring EBITA is flat at about EUR 1.4 billion rather than falling, and why EPS grows as restructuring and interest costs fall.

Capital allocation is the lever the market under-uses, and it is the chairman's known strength (he sold Saham's insurance arm to Sanlam for USD 1.1 billion in 2018). Two disposal options are live, and their effects are very different:

Strongest counter-case. Bull: a strategist chief executive with a clean sheet and a dealmaker chairman with his own money at risk deliver a low first guide, a sale above 8 times EBITA and a return of the proceeds. The company did guide conservatively and beat its initial objectives every year from 2018 to 2022 (Morgan Stanley).
Bear: a consultant-led reorganisation of a 490,000-person operation lets daily delivery slip, as happened at Atento. The global labour framework agreement has expired, and local negotiations became harder in mid-2026. A new restructuring programme above EUR 120 million arrives with the strategic update.

What would change my view. Better: restructuring guided at EUR 50 million or less; a signed disposal with a stated multiple and use of proceeds; an operator appointed as chief operating officer; insiders buying shares. Worse: a new restructuring programme above EUR 120 million; any unwinding of the chairman's exposure. The company has not disclosed whether the chairman's swap settled into shares at its maturity in September 2026. Morgan Stanley's own holding fell below 5% on 2026-09-08 through an off-market disposal, which is consistent with physical delivery of shares to Saham but does not prove it (my inference).

Against the market. The bulls (Bernstein) put disposals at the centre of the case: up to EUR 2.5 billion of proceeds, with EUR 1.8 billion returned to shareholders. The bears (Morgan Stanley) assume the proceeds go to debt and see no substantial buyback before FY2029. I side with the bears on the use of proceeds, because a board that bought back nothing at five times earnings has shown its preference. I side with the bulls in thinking the portfolio holds value that the price ignores. I differ from both in thinking the small TLScontact sale is the better first step, because it gives the signal of value without the dilution.

Score: 47, set by the Rater. The change is large and funded but repair-only: a new CEO, CFO and Chief AI Officer, Future Forward raised to EUR 150-170m of run-rate savings, tax down to 29%, refinancing and debt reduction, yet the savings only offset about 1.7 points a year of erosion, the new team reconfirmed then cut the FY2026 guide, restructuring recurs every second year, no disposal has come from the portfolio review and executives sold shares weeks before the cut. Real dated positives offset by present problems sit just below 50 (levels), as the group's 46 says; the capital-allocation option (TLScontact, early buybacks) is undated, so between Hexatronic 50 and Indus Holding 45.

#3Industry structure, competitive advantage, financial profile and management: a mid-quality business with one high-quality asset

Conclusion: the industry structure and business model are below average (no pricing power, and a substitute that sets the price), the cash profile is above average, and management is new and unproven on revenue: a medium-to-low quality foundation with a real cash floor.

Evidence.

  • Structure. Teleperformance and Concentrix each hold 9-10% of outsourced customer experience; the next two, Foundever and Telus Digital, hold 4% and 2%. The top five hold 20-27%, and 60-65% of customer care is still done in-house. The in-house and automated alternatives, not the two leaders, set the price. Competitors defend volume with discounts.
  • Advantage. Teleperformance operates in nearly 100 countries and 400 languages, holds compliance certifications and keeps long relationships (the top 100 clients have stayed 14 years on average). These strengths keep other labour-based providers out. They do not stop a client automating. Teleperformance rents its technology layer from cloud and model providers, or holds it through minority stakes worth EUR 25.9 million.
  • The one moat. LanguageLine, about three quarters of Specialized Services, is protected by legal mandates for human interpreters in US healthcare and courts. Even at LanguageLine, the price per minute has been lowered, and the margin gains came from cost.
  • Financial profile. Gross margin is 22%. The group recurring EBITA margin was 14.5% in FY2025, but the Core Services margin fell from 12.4% (FY2024) to 11.9% and then 10.5% in H1 2026, while the Specialized Services margin rose to 33.0%. Return on invested capital is about 10-11% including goodwill. Capital expenditure is about 2% of sales. Free cash flow averaged 9.5% of sales over four years, against 7% at Concentrix, with a margin about two points higher and lower leverage (net debt of EUR 4,013 million at June 2026, 2.1 times EBITDA on the company's lease-inclusive definition).
  • Earnings quality. FY2025 adjusted EPS on the brokers' basis was EUR 13.20; reported EPS was EUR 8.48. Restructuring, labelled non-recurring, came in every second year: EUR 13 million in FY2023, 112 million in FY2024, 16 million in FY2025 and about 140 million in FY2026.
  • Management and culture. Agent attrition is 66-68% a year, against 45-55% at the best competitors. Incentives were built on headcount. Ethics-hotline reports doubled in 2025. Revenue guidance has been cut four years running (#4).

Inference. Teleperformance is a mid-quality business with one high-quality asset, LanguageLine, inside it. Size buys staying power: a place on shrinking vendor panels, credibility on compliance, and the means to fund EUR 140 million of restructuring in a year. Size does not buy pricing power.

So what. For your setups, I would class Teleperformance as medium quality at best, non-cyclical and structurally questioned. "Reversion to normal" cannot mean the 16 times median multiple of an era of 8% organic growth. The financial profile supports a floor (cash, and a 6.3% dividend yield covered about three times by free cash flow), not a premium.
Strongest counter-case. Up: scaled operators end up as the orchestrators of human-plus-AI service, and compliance plus 14-year relationships make Teleperformance the natural integrator; outcome-based work is already over 15% of revenue and growing.
Down: Teleperformance's strengths are barriers, not advantages. As AI codifies workflows, switching costs fall and contracts move to annual renewal; the Core Services margin keeps losing 50-100 basis points a year; and a sale of Specialized Services would leave a single-segment group earning a 10-12% margin.

What would change my view. Better: the Core Services margin stabilising at 11.3-11.5% in FY2027; the outcome-based share of revenue moving towards 25% with a disclosed margin. Worse: a Core Services margin below 10% in H1 2027; a fall in the tenure of the top 100 clients.

Against the market. A multiple of five times earnings says "melting ice cube". I agree that Core Services has no moat and no pricing power. I differ on stability. With more than 1,500 clients and a variable cost base, the group's recurring margin has stayed between 14.4% and 15.1% since 2021, while organic growth swung from +25.7% to about -2%. Earnings are steadier than the multiple implies.

Score: 30, set by the Rater. Qualitatively weak: the largest player (9-10%) in a fragmented chain where in-house and automated alternatives set the price, barriers rather than advantages against AI, no pricing power, a Core margin falling from 12.4% to 10.5%, 66-68% agent attrition and a revenue guide cut four years running, with LanguageLine the one moat and possibly for sale; the figures (ROIC 6.2%, 46th percentile; EPS down 8% a year over three years, 27th) are flattered by acquisition-heavy deployment (61% of capital since FY2020) earning poorly, while cash conversion (free cash flow/net income at the 85th percentile), diversification and a stable recurring margin are the real floor. Coherent with the groups' 27/24/38/40; between Solid State 33 and Ithaca Energy 28.

#4Conservatism of guidance, and the record of delivery and upgrades: optimistic on revenue, reliable on cost and cash

Conclusion: guidance is not conservative and there has been no record of raising it since 2022, but the reset of the FY2027 guide and the 2028 targets is the one dated chance for that to change, and it can be judged on the day.

Evidence.

  • Revenue guidance. Each first revenue guide since 2023 (timeline above) leaned on the second half of the year, and each was cut in the second half.
  • Cost and cash guidance. Teleperformance has delivered on cost and cash: margins have ended within about 50 basis points of the first guide, and FY2024 free cash flow beat consensus.
  • The FY2026 guide is realistic, not conservative. Like-for-like growth for the first nine months is about -1.5%, so the range implies a fourth quarter between about -1.5% and -5.5%. Brokers sit at -1.7% to -2.9%, and the model at about -3.0%. The margin target was reaffirmed with seven weeks of the year left.
  • The 2028 targets (like-for-like growth of 4-6%, a margin of about 15.5%, EUR 3 billion of cumulative free cash flow, leverage of 1.2 times) stand far above every forecast. Management has said it will revisit them at a strategic update in the first half of 2027.
  • Pay. The executives' long-term incentive plan pays on cumulative free cash flow "over EUR 2.3 billion". The model's cumulative free cash flow for 2026-2028 is EUR 2.33 billion (the plan's exact definition and period are not in my files).
  • The sell-side has not been steered down gently. Consensus FY2026 EPS has fallen about 35% in three years, and consensus FY2028 EPS by 23% in twelve months; in July 2026, management spoke of "early success in our structural turnaround".

Inference. Today's guidance contains no conservatism, and the record on revenue is one of optimism. Three facts keep me from extrapolating that record into the FY2027 guide:

  1. The executives' own pay hurdle already sits where our forecast does, so the people setting targets know the realistic number.
  2. A chief executive and finance director who have just been embarrassed by an inherited guide have every reason to set a base they can beat.
  3. The board will write the first FY2027 guide knowing that first-half like-for-like growth is about -2.3%.

So what: the route to conservative guidance runs through the reset, and the reset can be judged on the day. I expect a like-for-like range of about -2% to 0%, a "stable" margin, restructuring of EUR 50-80 million and no buyback. I put the probability that the FY2027 guide survives 2027 uncut at a little better than even (about 55%), a cut at about 35% and a raise at about 10%.

Strongest counter-case. Sceptic: four first guides in a row were too high; former executives describe a commercial organisation that over-promises; growth outside T&S is slowing as the guide is written; and margins are published only twice a year, leaving the same eight-month blind interval in which the July reconfirmation and the November cut of 2026 took place.
Optimist: the 2018-2022 habit of guiding low and beating returns under a team that owns none of the old targets.

What would change my view. The guide itself, and whether it comes with a bridge: price, volume, offshoring and T&S for revenue; savings kept against savings passed on to clients for the margin. A guide with a bridge deserves weight. A guide without one does not.

Against the market. The market expects the reset and will discount any target until Teleperformance has met one. I agree. My one difference is of degree: I give more weight than the market narrative does to the chance that the first guide is set deliberately low, because the incentives changed with the people. I give that chance no weight in the forecasts.

Score: 20, set by the Rater. Revenue guidance cut in each of 2023, 2024, 2025 (twice) and 2026, each first guide leaning on a second half that then failed, the latest cut by the new team after a July reconfirmation, consensus FY2026 EPS down about 35% in three years and 2028 targets far above any forecast; margin and cash guides delivered within about 50 basis points keep it off the bottom. Exactly the levels' 25 description of expectations cut in consecutive years with no upgrade since, coherent with the Guidance group's 20; the reset in February is a chance, not a record, so between Indutrade 33 and TT Electronics 15.

#5Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost scope and feedback loops: the only amplifiers are financial

Conclusion: the business model has no pricing power and little operating leverage, so profit will not outgrow revenue; the only amplifiers are financial (debt paydown, then buybacks at a very low multiple), and they work on EPS, not on EBITA.

Evidence and inference, lever by lever.

None
Pricing power		None in Core Services, and negative in practice: clients take the productivity gains at renewal. Specialized Services defends its margin through cost, not price.
Low
Operating leverage to volume		Personnel costs are about 70% of Core Services revenue, and attrition of two thirds a year lets headcount follow volume within weeks. The contribution margin on a euro of volume is 25-30%. The record gives 10-15 basis points of group margin for each point of organic growth: in 2021, like-for-like growth of 25.7% lifted the margin by 230 basis points.
High
Leverage to price		A point of price is worth about three times as much EPS as a point of volume (#9).
Large gross, small net
Cost scope		The savings programme is worth 1.5-1.7% of revenue with a payback of about a year, but Teleperformance keeps about a third of the savings or less. The precedent search found no labour-based customer-experience provider that expanded its margin through a cost programme while revenue was flat or falling. The providers that raised margins were growing (Genpact, Firstsource, Ibex).
Amplifier
Financial leverage		Financial leverage amplifies the equity value more than EPS. Net debt including leases is about half of enterprise value, so a 5% shortfall in EBITDA at a constant EV/EBITDA multiple takes about 10% off the market value, and a 5% beat adds about 10%.
2 negative 1 positive
Feedback loops		Two loops are negative: the treadmill (price given back, a savings programme to replace it, restructuring to pay for the programme, then the next renewal) and the impairment loop (market value near book value, a goodwill test, a write-down, a headline; #7). One loop is positive: free cash flow cuts debt, the board restarts buybacks, and at about five times earnings each EUR 100 million retires about 2.4% of the shares. The positive loop starts in FY2029 in the model.
So what. In Teleperformance's model, revenue growth does not produce outsized profit growth: flat revenue produces flat profit. The amplifier sits in the capital structure and the share count, which is how EPS grows 5-6% a year with no operating growth. A buyback at five times earnings is worth more than any operating lever the company holds. The asymmetry to remember is that the cost structure which mutes volume risk magnifies price risk.
Strongest counter-case. Bull: outcome-based pricing lets the company keep productivity gains; individual experts claim margins above 60% on agentic resolution, and operating leverage would reappear if 25-30% of revenue moved to outcome-based pricing.
Bear: outcome-based contracts move delivery risk onto a workforce with two-thirds annual attrition, and Concentrix says such contracts "have not gained the momentum" it hoped for.

What would change my view. A disclosed margin on outcome-based work; an H1 2027 recurring margin of 14.0% or better (savings kept) rather than 13.6% (no savings kept); the board bringing buybacks forward.

Against the market. The sell-side also models a flat margin (13.9% to 14.5% for FY2027), so the Street and I agree that there is no operating leverage. What the Street has not modelled is the balance sheet. Consensus holds net debt flat at about EUR 4.97 billion with no buybacks to FY2028. The model has net debt falling by about EUR 0.9 billion between end-2026 and end-2028, and EUR 500 million of buybacks in FY2029-FY2030.

Score: 30, set by the Rater. The structure has little useful gearing and some working against it: no pricing power in Core (negative in practice), personnel about 70% of revenue with headcount following volume within weeks (25-30% contribution margin, 10-15 basis points of margin per point of growth), high gearing only to a price the company cannot set (a point of price is about three times a point of volume), and a cost programme mostly passed on; the forecast EPS-to-revenue ratio is meaningless on flat revenue. The only positive loop is financial (free cash flow to debt, then buybacks at about five times retiring 2.4% of shares per EUR 100m), which lifts it slightly above the levels' 25, consistent with the groups' 38 and 32.

#6Forecast financials: a flat business whose EPS grows only from below the operating line

Conclusion: the forecasts show a flat business whose clean EPS grows about 5-6% a year entirely from below the operating line, with no scope for double-digit growth, or for higher growth or margins than in the past, unless clients start paying for something new.

Note on FY2026 EPS growth. The model summary shows FY2026 EPS growth of +24.1%, but that figure is a change of basis, not growth (end note 1). On a like basis, FY2026 clean EPS is roughly 5-10% lower than FY2025 on my estimate, because restructuring rises to EUR 140 million from EUR 16-30 million. Adjusted EPS, before restructuring, rises about 5-7% on lower tax and interest. Two open queries on free cash flow and net debt are in end notes 2 and 3; on either figure, leverage does not reach the 1.2 times target before the end of 2029 without a disposal.

What the numbers say.

  • Shape. Revenue is flat across five years. Recurring EBITA is flat at about EUR 1.4 billion. Clean EPS grows 5.8% a year from FY2026 to FY2030, and 4.9% a year from FY2026 to FY2029.
  • Where the EPS growth comes from, FY2026 to FY2029 (my arithmetic on the model; total +EUR 1.94 a share). Restructuring falls from EUR 140 million to EUR 50 million, worth +EUR 1.08. Net financial costs fall from EUR 240 million to EUR 189 million, worth +EUR 0.62. A share count about 2% lower adds +EUR 0.29. Operations subtract EUR 0.06.

FY2027 alone: clean EPS rises EUR 0.62, but adjusted EPS, which ignores restructuring, does not grow at all (about EUR 14.1 to 14.0).

  • The 2027 half-years. In H1 2027, revenue falls 1.3% (like-for-like about -2.3%) at a recurring margin of about 13.6%, flat on a year earlier. In H2 2027, revenue rises 0.5% (like-for-like about +0.3%) at a margin of about 15.0%. Like-for-like growth steps up by about 2.6 points between the two halves with no change in the underlying business.
  • Against consensus. The model's revenue is 0.2%, 1.3% and 1.3% below consensus for FY2026-FY2028. EBITDA before restructuring is in line for FY2026 and about 1% and 3% below after that. Free cash flow is above consensus in FY2026 and 10-16% below after that, mostly because the model keeps the restructuring cash that several brokers drop. The model's clean EPS is 7%, 5% and 5% below the blended consensus median, while its adjusted equivalents (about EUR 14.1, 14.0 and 14.3) are slightly above.

The forecasts offer no scope for double-digit growth, or for more growth than in the past. Revenue grew about 11% a year from 2019 to 2025, mostly by acquisition, and the margin peaked at 15.1% in 2021. The next four years are slower on both measures. Double-digit EPS growth would need buybacks of roughly EUR 300 million a year at today's price (my estimate). Free cash flow after the dividend, about EUR 500 million a year, could fund buybacks of that size, but only if the board stopped putting debt reduction first.

So what. The earnings base is credible because it asks nothing of the revenue engine. The growth on top of the base is only as reliable as the board's restraint on restructuring.
Strongest counter-case. Up: the FY2027 margin range runs to 14.7% if savings and currency gains are kept, restructuring could be EUR 50 million, and a small disposal could start buybacks a year early; together these would add about 6% to FY2027 EPS and 8-9% to FY2028 EPS (my arithmetic from #9).
Down: the forecast sits on consensus for EBITDA, and EBITDA forecasts on consensus have been too high for four years running.

What would change my view. The H1 2027 margin and the restructuring guide (#7).

Against the market. The sell-side agrees with the flat shape of the forecasts. It has not said that operations contribute nothing to EPS growth, and its free cash flow for FY2027-FY2028 is too high unless restructuring stops.

Score: 51, set by the Rater. 5-10% gives C; placed at the floor because operations contribute nothing (all FY2026-29 growth is falling restructuring 56%, falling interest 32% and a lower share count 15%), the recurring margin drifts down from 14.4% to 14.1% below its 15.1% peak, adjusted EPS does not grow in FY2027, and on a like basis FY2026 is below FY2025, so the real growth is thinner than the measure (consensus 3.6%, 10.9th percentile).

#7Scope for upgrades to guidance, estimates and the narrative over 6-12 months: negative until July 2027

Conclusion: scope for upgrades over the next six months is negative, with cuts more likely than not at each event to July 2027; it turns neutral-to-positive in months nine to eighteen, when the base effect, a lower restructuring line and a guide that is met could bring the first upgrades in four years.

Inference: the skew of estimate changes is to cuts until July 2027, for three reasons. Consensus has not yet absorbed Morgan Stanley's 8% cut of 2026-11-12. Five of ten brokers still have FY2027 revenue growing 0.8% to 2.0%. Price targets (mean EUR 77.58) have not followed estimates down. The cuts still to come are small for EBITDA (1-3%) and largest for free cash flow (10-16%). Brokers who exclude restructuring from EPS are already at our numbers.

What is not yet in the numbers or the narrative.

Positive

A low restructuring year (EUR 50 million adds about 3% to clean EPS). The currency tailwind. The optical step-up in growth between the two halves of 2027. A small disposal at a high multiple. The balance sheet (#5).

Negative

The later-than-expected T&S base effect. The fading of the savings contribution in H2 2027. A reset that comes in two steps, results in February and targets later. An impairment test taken with market value within a few euros a share of book value: goodwill was EUR 4,283 million against equity of EUR 4,193 million at June 2026. I put the probability of some impairment charge at about even, and of a charge above EUR 500 million at about one in ten. Any charge would be non-cash, and the EUR 2.69 billion minimum-equity covenant in the private placements leaves about EUR 1.5 billion of headroom.
So what. For the next two results, "in line with the model" will read as a downgrade to consensus. The upgrade case starts only when three things can be seen together: a guide that is being met, a margin with savings in it, and a positive like-for-like quarter. The earliest date for all three is November 2027. The narrative upgrade on offer is modest but new: "decline disproved", not "growth restored".
Strongest counter-case. Positive: the February results are a full clean-up (a low guide, an impairment, a restructuring number), and the shares rise on the end of uncertainty. Adecco rose 8% on the day it halved its dividend in February 2025.
Negative: precedent puts 18-30 months between a reset of targets and the trough in consensus EPS (about 24 months at Worldline), which would place Teleperformance's trough in late 2028 or 2029, not 2027.

What would change my view. The three tests of 2027-02-25 (#0); growth outside T&S in Q4 2026 (+1.5% or better supports the base case; zero or below contradicts it); the H1 2027 margin.

Against the market. Bernstein expects low-to-mid single-digit downgrades to consensus EPS, and I agree. I am more specific about which line is most exposed (free cash flow) and about when the direction of revisions can turn (not before late July 2027).

Score: 20, set by the Rater. Guidance, which counts most, faces a reset: the 2028 targets are likely to be cut or re-dated at the H1 2027 update and the first FY2027 guide carries a 35% cut against a 10% raise chance; consensus, next, has about an 80% chance of being lower by February and 50% lower again by July (free cash flow cuts 10-16%, EPS low-to-mid single digits), which against near-zero revenue growth is a large negative ratio; the narrative upgrade ('decline disproved') is back-loaded to months nine to twelve at the earliest. Coherent with the group's 25 but nearer the levels' 10 on guidance, between Xvivo 23 and Yara 17.

#8Current momentum in guidance, estimates, narrative, price and peers: split, and the split cannot last

Conclusion: momentum in guidance, estimates and narrative is strongly negative and the closest peers offer no lift; only the price trend is positive, and it rests on a 2026 re-rating that the November cut has already stalled.

Evidence.

  • Sell-side estimates. FY2027 consensus EPS is down 3% over one and three months and 9% over twelve; consensus EBITDA and sales are each down 2% over three months. The share of buy ratings is 20%, down 7 points in three months and 20 points in six. Morgan Stanley moved to Underweight on 2026-11-12.
  • Narrative. Morgan Stanley's title, "Structural headwinds intensifying", captures the market narrative.
  • Price. The share price is up 52% over nine months, 18.2% above its 200-day average and at the 71st percentile of relative strength. But the price is flat over three and six months, fell about 15% on the guidance cut, and sits below its 50-day average of EUR 73.27. The 200-day average has risen in only four of the last twelve months.
  • Co-movement. Over six months, the sector basket explains only 8% of the stock's daily moves. The stock trades on its own news and on news about the automation of customer service.
  • Peers. Concentrix reported revenue down 1.2% in its third quarter and a second goodwill impairment (USD 1.05 billion), traded at a forward P/E of 2.3 times in October 2026, and has an activist on the register. TaskUs is growing outside its largest client, Meta, with AI services up 28%, and is valued at about four times earnings. Telus Digital has been taken private. The wider dashboard sector has no common trend.

Inference: either estimates stabilise after the reset, or the price gives back its 2026 re-rating. The price momentum was earned between February and July 2026 on a change of governance: the multiple rose from about 3.3 times to 4.8 times while estimates fell. Earnings momentum carries the worst grade there is. The fall on 2026-11-05 shows which way the adjustment runs on a disappointment.

So what. Nothing in the current momentum qualifies as strong upgrade momentum. The A rating for technical momentum is a memory of the summer, and it is likely to be downgraded if the price stays below its 50-day average.

Strongest counter-case. The shares have kept most of the year's gain through a guidance cut and a broker downgrade, which suggests that sellers are tiring. Long-only ownership has thinned (active institutional ownership of about 70%, against 89% in 2020, per Morgan Stanley), and four brokers in five do not rate the stock a buy. Clearing events work from exactly that positioning.

What would change my view. A revision score above zero; a rising share of buy ratings; the price back above its 50-day average on a good result for growth outside T&S.

Against the market. I have no difference with the market here: the dashboard's letter ratings describe the momentum accurately.

Score: 50, set by the Rater. Both measures positive would give B, but the parts strongly contradict the stale sell-side reading: guidance cut on 2026-11-05, FY2027 EPS down 3% over one and three months, the buy share down 7 points in three months and 20 in six, the dashboard's revision score -11 (F) and a fresh Morgan Stanley Underweight, the price below its 50-day average and peers (Concentrix) negative, so the letter moves one step to C and sits at the band's floor.

#9Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts: simple to state, hard to monitor

Conclusion: the case is simple to state and hard to monitor, with a moderate, downward-leaning earnings cone of about ±10% for FY2027 and a far wider share-price cone, driven by sudden, sentiment-led events and by a multiple that precedent says can go lower before it goes higher.

The case is simple to state: two operating variables (growth outside T&S; the recurring margin) and two board variables (restructuring; capital return). The case is hard to monitor: margins appear twice a year, and price, contract length and the share of revenue up for renewal are not disclosed at all.

The five judgements, with the arithmetic. The FY2027 base is the model's: revenue EUR 9,914 million, recurring EBITA of about EUR 1,418 million (14.3%), pre-tax profit EUR 1,089 million, tax at 29.5%, net income EUR 768 million, about 58.7 million shares, clean EPS EUR 13.09 and free cash flow EUR 780 million. All the figures below are my arithmetic.

  1. The margin holds, because savings and currency cover the price given back.
    • Core Services revenue is about EUR 8.5 billion. One further point of price, not matched by productivity, removes EUR 85 million of revenue and no cost.
    • Recurring EBITA falls to EUR 1,333 million (-6.0%), and the margin falls to 13.6% (1,333 / 9,829).
    • Pre-tax profit falls to EUR 1,004 million; net income falls EUR 60 million to EUR 708 million; EPS falls EUR 1.02 to EUR 12.07 (-7.8%).
    • Free cash flow falls by about EUR 60 million, and year-end leverage rises by about 0.1 times.
    • Expressed as margin, each 10 basis points is worth EUR 9.9 million of EBITA and EUR 0.12 of EPS (0.9%). The brokers' FY2027 margin range of 13.9% (Deutsche Bank) to 14.5% (Bernstein, Redburn) therefore spans -3.7% to +1.8% around the model's EPS.
  2. Growth outside T&S holds near +0.5%, and no second vertical is automated in one step.
    • Growth two points lower removes EUR 198 million of revenue; at a 27.5% contribution margin, EBITA falls EUR 55 million (-3.9%) and the margin to 14.0%; net income falls EUR 39 million and EPS EUR 0.66 (-5.0%). Growth two points higher has the symmetrical effect.
    • A step loss of a client programme worth 4% of revenue removes EUR 397 million of revenue and EUR 109 million of EBITA (more if the work is high-margin, as T&S was); net income falls EUR 77 million and EPS EUR 1.31 (-10%). I accept the earlier Analyst's 15-25% probability of such a loss in any 18 months.
    • Point for point, volume costs about 2.5% of EPS and Core Services price about 8%.
  3. Restructuring falls to EUR 80 million in FY2027.
    • At EUR 140 million (a new programme), EBITDA falls EUR 60 million, net income EUR 42 million and EPS EUR 0.72 (-5.5%) to EUR 12.37, below FY2026, so the year's growth is gone. I put the probability of this outcome at about 15%.
    • At EUR 50 million (Morgan Stanley's assumption), EPS rises EUR 0.36 (+2.8%) to EUR 13.45.
    • Adjusted EPS is unchanged in both cases, which is why the same restructuring announcement will be a cut for some brokers and a non-event for others.
  4. Free cash flow goes to debt until FY2029 and to buybacks after that; there is no large disposal.
    • A EUR 200 million buyback one year early, at EUR 71.68. The buyback retires 2.79 million shares (4.7%) and costs EUR 6 million of after-tax interest, so FY2028 EPS rises 4%. With no buybacks at all, FY2030 EPS would be about 9% lower.
    • TLScontact sold for EUR 470 million, with the proceeds used to cut debt. The lost EBIT of about EUR 39 million (EUR 27.5 million after tax) outweighs the EUR 14.9 million of after-tax interest saved, so EPS falls 1.6%. Leverage falls by about 0.25 times, which brings the 1.2 times target, and with it the first buyback, forward by about a year.
    • Specialized Services sold for EUR 2.5 billion (Bernstein's figure, about 5.7 times EBITA). The sale loses EBITA of about EUR 438 million (EUR 309 million after tax) and saves interest at 4.5% before tax. The effect on EPS depends on the use of proceeds (tax on the gain and costs ignored):
      • All proceeds to debt: net income EUR 538 million, EPS EUR 9.18 (-30%), leverage about 0.6 times.
      • Half to debt and half to buybacks at EUR 75: 42.0 million shares, EPS EUR 11.88 (-9%).
      • Thirty per cent to debt and 70% to buybacks at EUR 75: 35.3 million shares, EPS EUR 13.67 (+4%), leverage about 1.9 times; at a buyback price of EUR 90, EPS EUR 12.31 (-6%).
      On adjusted EPS, the earlier Analyst's equivalents were -27%, -5% and +9%.
    • The lesson from the disposal arithmetic: at 5.7 times EBITA, the large sale transfers value to shareholders only if most of the proceeds buy back shares cheaply. Morgan Stanley's 8.5 times EBIT for LanguageLine would be well above the group's own multiple and would add value on any split of proceeds; price pressure at comparable language-services businesses (AMN's language revenue fell 8% in Q1 2026) is a reason to doubt that valuation.
  5. The market keeps paying about five times earnings until it has proof.
    • Two-year-forward EPS at end-2027 is FY2029's EUR 14.41, so each turn of the multiple is worth EUR 14.4 a share, 20% of today's price. No earnings line moves the value as much (#12).

The FY2027 earnings cone is roughly ±10% around the base case and leans down. The cases are bear EUR 11.3 (25% probability), base EUR 13.1 (50%), upside EUR 14.2 (20%) and bull EUR 15.0 (5%), which weight to EUR 13.0, or about EUR 12.8 after allowing for a step loss. The cone leans down because price is the largest sensitivity, restructuring has been raised before, and the step-loss tail has no upside equivalent.

The character of the risks.

  • Structural, not cyclical. The business held organic growth near zero through 2009-2010, so the recession playbook does not apply. The relevant precedents are disrupted labour-based outsourcers, which show trough multiples of 2-5 times forward earnings (TaskUs 4.0, Worldline 3.0, Capita 4.1, and Concentrix 2.3), re-rating only after several quarters of stable organic growth and a repaired balance sheet, and outcomes for weaker peers that run from a take-private (Telus Digital) to a debt-for-equity swap (Atento). Teleperformance is the best capitalised of the group, which is why it trades at the top of the trough range, and also why today's multiple is not a floor.
  • Market and country. Teleperformance is a leveraged French equity ahead of the spring 2027 presidential election.
So what. The earnings can be forecast to within about 10%; the share price cannot. The risks that matter are the multiple and the monitoring gap, and both are tied to dated events.
Strongest counter-case. Safer than it looks: the diffuse client base has held the group margin inside a 70 basis point band for five years, the largest shock is behind it, and at five times earnings a 10% miss is already paid for.
Riskier than it looks: the Core Services margin is the true series, it is falling, and the group margin survives only on a Specialized Services mix that is finite and for sale.

What would change my view. Quarterly margin disclosure, or a price bridge, would cut the monitoring risk more than any single result.

Against the market. The market treats the risk as existential, a question of terminal value. I see low solvency risk, moderate earnings risk and high multiple risk. The danger is less that the business breaks than that it cannot prove, for another year, that it is not breaking.

Score: 34, set by the Rater. The memo's FY2027 EPS cone is about plus or minus 10% leaning down (weighted EUR 12.8-13.0 against 13.1), and the case is simple to state (two operating and two board variables), but it is hard to track (half-yearly margins, no price or renewal disclosure), carries sudden, sentiment-led falls (-14% on Klarna, -34% on a labour event, -15% on the guide), a 15-25% tail of a step client loss and net debt about half of enterprise value; solvency risk is low. Coherent with the groups' 30 and 42; between D'Ieteren 38 and Helios Towers 33.

#10Where the stock is in its lifecycle: bottoming, not yet turning up

Conclusion: the stock is bottoming and not yet turning up: estimates are still falling, the first price turn stalled on the November cut, and the evidence that would confirm a turn is dated late July and early November 2027.

Evidence. The dashboard's rule places the stock at Turning/Inflecting, but that rule reads the share price (#8). The fundamentals read differently: guidance was cut eight days ago, estimates are still falling, the mid-term targets are about to be withdrawn, and the two data points that could confirm a turn are dated late July and early November 2027. The share price turned up in early 2026 on the change of governance and stalled on 2026-11-05.

Inference. The fundamentals are bottoming, and the price made a first turn that failed. I place the stock at bottoming, with a dated marker for each later phase:

So what. Bottoming is the phase in which forecasts are least certain and the fair multiple is lowest (#11). It is also the phase in which a low price can be right. The practical point is one of sequence: the proof comes after the reset, and the reset is more likely than not to lower estimates first.
Strongest counter-case. The stock is already turning: clean EPS troughs in FY2026 as restructuring peaks, the price low of EUR 42.66 is months behind, and multiples have historically bottomed before operations did.
Or the bottom is false, on the Concentrix pattern, where each reset is followed by another; growth outside T&S turning negative would move the phase to "collapsing".

What would change my view. Up a phase: two of the three tests of 2027-02-25 met, with growth outside T&S at +1% or better. Down a phase: growth outside T&S at or below zero, or a new restructuring programme above EUR 120 million.

Against the market. The dashboard says turning; Morgan Stanley's Underweight says still falling; Bernstein says trough. I sit between them: bottoming, with a first turn that failed.

Score: 38, set by the Rater. I agree with the memo, not the computed Turning/Inflecting: the price turn was a governance re-rating (3.3x to 4.8x while estimates fell) that stalled on the 2026-11-05 cut, guidance was cut eight days ago, estimates are still falling and the mid-term targets are about to go; the fundamentals are early bottoming, with the turn's evidence dated late July and November 2027 and a false-bottom (Concentrix) risk. Below Linea Directa's fair bottoming because estimates are still being cut, between National Grid 40 and D'Ieteren 35.

#11The fair multiple: 5-7 times now and 7-9 times on proof, far below the guideline's 18.89 times

Conclusion: the guideline's 18.89 times belongs to the company's growth era and is not supported by the forecasts; my view of fair is 5-7 times two-year-forward earnings while estimates are falling and 7-9 times once flat-to-positive organic growth is proven, which leaves today's 5.2 times at the low end.

The guideline. Viewforth's guideline sets the fair multiple at 18.89 times two-year-forward earnings: the 60th percentile of the stock's ten-year history, for a stock whose starting phase is Turning/Inflecting. The guideline multiple is 293% above the multiple on consensus (4.81 times) and 3.6 times the model's own 5.2 times. Topic #12 uses the guideline multiple.

My view of the guideline, in four steps.

  1. The guideline embeds a growth era. The ten-year range (median 16.4 times, 10th percentile 8.0 times) is dominated by 2016-2022, when organic growth averaged about 8% a year. The shares last traded at the guideline multiple in July 2022, at EUR 276, in a year for which the company guided to like-for-like growth above 12%. At month-ends, the multiple has not been above 9 times since April 2023, or above 7 times since January 2024.
  1. On the forecasts, the guideline multiple would mean the valuation of a growing compounder (my arithmetic): a price of about EUR 272, a market value of about EUR 16 billion, an enterprise value of about ten times EBITDA and a free cash flow yield of 4.9%, for a business with no growth. The forecasts do not describe a compounder.
  2. The evidence supports a far lower multiple.
    • The stock's recent range: a two-year median of 4.55 times and a five-year median of 5.87 times.
    • Precedent: 2-5 times at the trough for disrupted labour-based outsourcers (#9).
    • A perpetuity cross-check (my arithmetic; free cash flow is about equal to clean net income). Flat earnings at a 10-12% cost of equity are worth 8-10 times. Earnings declining 2% a year are worth 7-8 times. Morgan Stanley's 16% discount rate with no growth gives about 6 times. Today's 5.2 times implies a decline of 7-9% a year at a 10-12% cost of equity.
    • Earnings quality: the model's EPS is already after restructuring, so no further discount is needed for recurring restructuring.
  1. My range. 5-7 times while organic growth is negative and estimates are falling, which covers the next nine to twelve months. 7-9 times once two quarters of flat-to-positive organic growth and a met guide are on the record, in early 2028 at the soonest. More than 10 times would need evidence that clients pay for something new (an outcome-based share of revenue of 25% or more with a disclosed margin; organic growth of 3% or more), and that evidence is in nobody's forecast.
So what. The first leg of any re-rating, to 7 times, does not need a believer in growth. It needs four quarters without decline, and at 7 times the shares would still yield about 13% in free cash flow. That bar is low in absolute terms and real in time. Because the guideline's multiple is nearly three times the top of my near-term range, the return in #12 should be read as the output of a rule, not of the forecasts.
Strongest counter-case. Higher: outside recessions the stock traded at 15-25 times; Bernstein's reverse calculation in August 2026 found the price discounting a revenue fall of more than 20%; any stabilisation could re-rate the stock quickly.
Lower: Concentrix trades at 2.3 times; if earnings are re-based for a new restructuring programme or a sliding Core Services margin, 3.5 times on lower earnings gives EUR 42-50 a share.

What would change my view. Up: a positive like-for-like quarter and an H1 2027 margin of 14.0% or better; a disposal at a stated multiple above 8 times EBITA; a dated buyback. Down: negative growth outside T&S; a re-basing of clean earnings.

Against the market. The market pays about 5 times, the guideline says 18.89 times, and I say 5-7 times now and 7-9 times on proof. I agree with the market on today's level and disagree that today's level is right for the business the forecasts describe.

Score: 76, set by the Rater. Cheap on one and neutral on the other gives B; placed at the floor because most of the cheapness is deserved: the ten-year range comes from an 8% organic-growth era, the stock is bottoming with estimates still falling, disrupted peers trade at 2-5x, and the memo's own fair range of 5-7x leaves today's 5.2x only modestly below fair.

#12Total shareholder return: about +20% weighted to end-2027, with the large numbers coming only from re-rating

Conclusion: the model's +292.5% to end-2027 and +340.7% to mid-2029 are nine-tenths the guideline multiple; the forecasts themselves support dividends plus earnings growth of about +17% and +35%, with roughly 20 points more for each turn of re-rating and a loss of about 17% at a 3.5 times trough.

The model's return at the guideline fair multiple (share price EUR 71.68; multiple today 5.2 times; fair multiple 18.89 times, reached at the first horizon).

What drives each part of the return.

  • The multiple: nine-tenths of the return. The whole of the +263.9% is the move from 5.2 to 18.89 times. That move is the product of the guideline, not of anything in the forecasts (#11).
  • Earnings: +4.4% and +15.8%. Two-year-forward EPS rises from about EUR 13.8 today to EUR 14.41 (FY2029) at the first horizon and to about EUR 16.0 at the second. All of the rise comes from falling restructuring, falling interest and, from FY2029, EUR 500 million of buybacks (#6). The earnings part is reliable to about ±10%.
  • Dividends: +12.7% and +19.4%. The dividends are EUR 4.50, 4.60 and 4.80 a share, covered about three times by free cash flow, and they are the most dependable part of the return. One caution: the first horizon counts two dividends (EUR 9.10), but the company would pay the second in 2028, so an investor buying today collects one dividend, 6.3%, by end-2027 (end note 4).

Inference.

  • The forecasts support dividends plus earnings growth: about +17% to end-2027 and +35% to mid-2029, or 12-15% a year, with no re-rating at all. That return is what a 19% earnings yield delivers when the earnings hold.
  • Each turn of re-rating adds about 20 points of return.
  • The downside is a lower multiple on lower earnings. At 3.5 times, the return is about -17%. If EPS were also 14% lower (the bear case of #9), the value would be about EUR 52, or -27%. A Concentrix-style 2.3 times on unchanged earnings gives about EUR 42, close to the 52-week low of EUR 42.66.
  • A rough probability weighting (my illustration, below) gives about EUR 88, a return a little over +20% to end-2027, with a wide spread and the gains arriving late.

So what: the three parts of the return carry very different confidence.

Strongest counter-case. For a higher return: free cash flow after the dividend is about EUR 500 million a year, enough to buy back more than a fifth of the company in two years if the board chose, and buyback announcements moved the shares by up to 55% in late 2022 and 19% in 2025 (Morgan Stanley).
For a lower return: the earnings yield is only real if the earnings are, and a business that has cut its revenue guide four years running has not earned that trust.

What would change my view. Only the inputs to #9 (the earnings judgements) and #11 (the multiple) move the return.

Against the market. The FactSet target prices (mean EUR 77.58, median EUR 72.00, range EUR 45 to 105) imply no re-rating in twelve months. The model at the guideline multiple implies EUR 281. My reading is about EUR 84 to 110 a share including dividends by end-2027, if earnings arrive as forecast.

Score: 75, set by the Rater. About +21-23% sits low in the B band (about 77 on the scale); held at the floor because the central case rests on a modest re-rating that cannot be proven before late 2027, the gains are back-loaded, and the lower tail is fat (-27% in the bear case, about -41% at a Concentrix-style 2.3x); the model's +292.5% at the guideline multiple is disregarded, as the memo itself does.

#13Summary conclusion: a short, dated route from concern to clearing

Bottom lineTeleperformance is a flat, cash-rich, mid-quality business that the market values as a shrinking one. It is not yet one of your setups, but the route to one is short and dated, and the gains, when they come, come from a re-rating that needs no belief in growth.

The forecasts need no heroics. They assume no pricing power, no retained AI productivity and no disposal. They need the margin to hold and the board to stop spending on restructuring. Those modest requirements make the earnings base believable, and they make the growth on top of the base small, financial and discretionary.

Today, outcomes and upgrades are not skewed to the positive. For six to nine months, the skew of estimate changes is negative, the momentum in estimates is the worst there is, and the business cannot prove its stability before late 2027.

What makes Teleperformance worth your attention is that the route from here to one of your setups is short and dated. A first guide set low and then met, a margin that shows savings being kept, and one positive quarter would turn a cause for concern into a clearing one, at a multiple where four quarters without decline would justify a re-rating of a third or more. The capital-allocation options (a small disposal at a high multiple, an earlier buyback) sit on top, and they are in nobody's numbers.

The work now is to watch three dates: 2027-02-25, late July 2027 and early November 2027.

A price-taker in a structurally questioned industry with a falling Core margin and returns on recent capital below its cost (topic 3, 30), with a four-year record of revenue guide cuts (topic 4, 20), held off the bottom by real cash conversion, 1,500-plus clients, a recurring margin held at 14.4-15.1% since 2021 and LanguageLine's mandated moat; the levels' 25 (Maersk 30, Alfen 25).
Setups' Fit/Crispness: 45, set by the Rater.

Case Riskiness: 28, set by the Rater.
Over topic 9's 34, Richard's Judges Scientific red flags apply and compound: an end market under disruption, a consultant CEO with no industry profit-and-loss experience following a founder of nearly 50 years, and an acquisition-heavy past (61% of capital since FY2020) with restructuring every second year, on net debt of about half of enterprise value and with half-yearly blind intervals; the low multiple in its range and an operating EPS cone of about 10% keep it above Judges' 20.

End notes

How to read this memo

  • Terms. Like-for-like (LFL) growth is revenue growth at constant currency and scope. T&S is Trust & Safety, the content-moderation vertical. Core Services is customer care, technical support, back office and T&S (about 86% of revenue); Specialized Services is LanguageLine interpretation, TLScontact visa services and Health Advocate. H1 and H2 are the first and second halves of a year; Q1 to Q4 are its quarters.
  • Three earnings bases, never mixed. Recurring EBITA is the company's guided line, before restructuring. Clean EPS is the model's EPS: after restructuring, before amortisation of acquired intangibles. Adjusted EPS is the brokers' usual figure, also before restructuring. The FactSet consensus EPS blends brokers on both definitions, so a "beat" or "miss" has to be read broker by broker.
  • "My arithmetic" marks a figure I calculated from the model or the files. Probabilities are judgements, not measurements.
  • The forecasts. All forecasts are those of the Financial Analyst's model (update 2). I changed no forecast input, because the earlier Analyst's changes of 2026-11-13 already carry the three AlphaSense reports written for this memo and Morgan Stanley's cut of 2026-11-12. I tested each line against that evidence and found nothing that moves a line by more than the forecast's own margin of error.
  • Limits of the evidence. The sell-side narrative rests on four houses read in depth (Morgan Stanley, Bernstein, Deutsche Bank, Rothschild & Co Redburn). Evidence on what investors themselves think is thin. The next results date, 2027-02-25, is FactSet's and is unconfirmed.

Notes on the forecasts

  1. FY2026 EPS growth. The model summary's FY2026 EPS growth of +24.1% reflects a change of basis: the FY2025 history is struck after EUR 218 million of acquired-intangible amortisation and at a tax rate near 38%, while the forecast is struck before that amortisation and at 29.5%.
  2. Free cash flow. The earlier Analyst's own cross-check of free cash flow is about EUR 30 million a year lower than the model's.
  3. Net debt. The earlier Analyst believes the model's net debt counts one dividend twice in FY2026, which would overstate leverage by about 0.15 times in every year; the query is open with the Financial Analyst.
  4. Dividend timing. The double-counted dividend in the first-horizon return of #12 is part of the earlier Analyst's open query on dividend timing.
